news.title: Agbagu Warns Flamingos Against Brazil’s Threats Ahead of U-17 World Cup Semi-Final Clash
news.lede: Nigeria Football Coaches Association (NFCA), Ogun State Chapter Chairman, Agbagu Damilola Victor, has urged the Flamingos to remain focused and cautious ahead of their semi-final encounter against Brazil at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Speaking in an interview with Sports247 following Nigeria’s 1-0 quarter-final victory over Venezuela, Agbagu praised head coach Akeem Busari and his technical crew for their tactical approach, commitment and contribution to the team’s impressive progress. Read Also: Can Flamingos Beat Brazil On Wednesday In Women’s U17 World Cup Semi-final, After 1-0 Win Over Venezuela? The Choosen Generation Angels Manager commended Busari and his assistants for guiding the young Nigerian side to the last four, while acknowledging the work being done behind the scenes to develop the players.

news.title: Nkwocha Wins Player of the Match as Nigeria’s Flamingos Edge Venezuela to Reach U-17 World Cup Semi-Finals
news.lede: Nigeria’s 17-year-old midfielder, Favour Chiamaka Nkwocha, has been named Player of the Match following the Flamingos’ narrow 1-0 victory over Venezuela in the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Sunday. Sports247 reports that the FC Robo Queens midfielder earned a starting role under head coach Akeem Busari and played her part as Nigeria secured a place in the semi-finals of the tournament. Read Also: Can Flamingos Beat Brazil On Wednesday In Women’s U17 World Cup Semi-final, After 1-0 Win Over Venezuela? Born on April 27, 2009, Nkwocha is regarded as one of the emerging talents in Nigerian women’s football.

news.title: Can Flamingos Beat Brazil On Wednesday In Women’s U17 World Cup Semi-final, After 1-0 Win Over Venezuela?
news.lede: Nigeria’s female cadet national team, Flamingos will tango Brazil this Wednesday in the semi-finals of the 2026 FIFA Women’s U-17 World Cup in Morocco, Sports247 reports. This is sequel to an 89th minute lone goal from the Nigerian captain, Azeezat Oduntan through a penalty kick that gave Coach Akeem Busari’s team a 1-0 win over Venezuela in Sunday’s quarter-finals. Read Also: “Brazil Must Be Ready for Nigeria” — SSA Adeboye Hails Flamingos, Backs Girls for Historic World Cup Final. The feat sent Flamingos’ fans into frenzy late Sunday, as many took to social media to celebrate the semi-final ticket, which brought back memories of how the squad of 2022 handled by Bankole Olowookere won bronze at that year’s competition in India.

news.title: [Official] "World Cup Debut" Kim Hyeon-jun's Final 21-Man Squad Confirmed... "Sole 2010 Birth Year" Im Ji-seong Selected, First Match Against Uganda on the 19th
news.lede: The South Korean Under-17 (U-17) football national team, led by Coach Kim Hyeon-jun, will challenge for a spot on the World Cup main stage. On the 2nd, the Korea Football Association announced, "We have finalized the final list of 21 players for the men's U-17 football national team that will participate in the 2026 International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) U-17 World Cup to be held in Qatar starting on the 19th." The final squad for the U-17 national team led by Coach Kim Hyeon-jun includes three goalkeepers, seven defenders, nine midfielders, and two forwards. Most of the players who participated in the UEFA Friendship Cup held in Switzerland last September were included.

news.title: All White Tommy Smith’s former club chase World Cup payments
news.lede: The owner of English club Braintree Town says football authorities owe them significant sums of money following former player Tommy Smith’s involvement in the FIFA Men’s World Cup. Braintree chairman Lee Harding has raised concerns about outstanding payments, according to a report in the Colchester Gazette. “Our club are still owed money, lots of it, hundreds of thousands of pounds, by The FA, UEFA and FIFA,” said Harding. The issue centres on money the National League club believe they are entitled to receive following Smith’s selection for New Zealand’s World Cup squad.

news.title: England’s Rugby Football League creates development panel after World Cup exit — BBC Sport
news.lede: England’s Rugby Football League (RFL) has announced the creation of the One Game, One England panel to prepare a plan for developing the game after England’s men’s and women’s teams failed to progress beyond the group stage of the Rugby League World Cup. Former Great Britain captain Paul Sculthorpe, retiring England women’s captain Jodie Cunningham and former international Adrian Morley will take part in its work, BBC Sport reports. England’s men’s team won two of their three group-stage matches and finished with a points difference of +86, but that was not enough to reach the play-offs. Their elimination was finally confirmed after Tonga defeated Samoa 20-18.
